identity.title: ALMA-IRDC - II. First high-angular resolution measurements of the <SUP>14</SUP>N/<SUP>15</SUP>N ratio in a large sample of infrared-dark cloud cores
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the first interferometric survey of the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio in N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ obtained with Atacama Large Millimeter Array observations towards four infrared-dark clouds harbouring 3 mm continuum cores associated with different physical properties.

Observations have been performed with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) towards the sample of IRDCs described in Barnes et al. in prep. (hereafter paper I). The project IDs are 2017.1.00687.S and 2018.1.00850.S (PI: A.T. Barnes).

question.value: What is the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio in N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ at high angular resolution across dense cores in infrared-dark clouds, and how does it relate to surrounding diffuse gas and core physical or evolutionary properties?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we present the first interferometric study of the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio towards a large sample of IRDC cores in N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ at high-angular resolution.

In particular, because each core is classified as starless or star-forming within each cloud, we are also able to compare the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratios with the presence/absence of protostellar activity.
The project IDs are 2017.1.00687.S and 2018.1.00850.S (PI: A.T. Barnes).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00687.S & ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00850.S.
The project IDs are 2017.1.00687.S and 2018.1.00850.S (PI: A.T. Barnes).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00687.S & ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00850.S.

We present the first interferometric survey of the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio in N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ obtained with Atacama Large Millimeter Array observations towards four infrared-dark clouds harbouring 3 mm continuum cores associated with different physical properties.

findings_qualitative.value: N15NH+ (1-0) emission is preferentially detected towards cores with strong 3 mm continuum emission, typically located in the central parts of the clouds (except in Cloud F).

evidence.loc: 3.1.1 Extraction of the spectra and line detection
evidence.quote: The N$^{15}$NH$^+$ emission is preferentially detected towards cores with strong continuum emission (cores C2c3/5, C2c4, C2c6 in Cloud C; core D7c3 in Cloud D; Cores F1c1, F1c2, F1c3, F4c5, F4c7 in Cloud F; cores H3c3 and H5c3 in Cloud H), and are usually located in the central part of the cloud, with the exception of the cores in Cloud F, located at the southern and northern edge of the cloud (Fig. 1).

findings_qualitative.value: The 14N/15N ratio in compact dense continuum cores is lower on average (~210) and spans a narrower range (~80-400) than in single-dish surveys or the ALMA total power data alone, indicating that 14N/15N is higher in the diffuse surrounding envelopes due to selective photodissociation.

evidence.quote: The spread of values is narrower than that found in any previous single-dish survey of high-mass star-forming regions, and than that obtained using the total power data only. This suggests that the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio is on average higher in the diffuse gaseous envelope of the cores

In all cores except F1c1, which is the most extended one, the beam-averaged $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratios are larger by a factor $\sim 1.5 - 3$ than those obtained in the embedded cores at higher angular resolution.

findings_qualitative.value: Evolutionary stage (starless vs star-forming classification) does not play a significant role in nitrogen fractionation of N2H+.

evidence.quote: However, given the large dispersions, we confirm overall the result suggested by previous works (Fontani et al. (cite: fontani15), Zeng et al. (cite: zeng17), Colzi et al. (cite: colzi18a), (cite: colzi18b)): time does not seem to play a role in the enrichment, or depletion, of $^{15}$N in N$_{2}$H$^{+}$.

findings_qualitative.value: There are no strong correlations between 14N/15N and core physical properties, consistent with gas-phase chemical models (Roueff et al. 2015; Loison et al. 2019), aside from tentative positive trends with H2 column density and (in star-forming cores) sonic Mach number and dust temperature.

evidence.quote: Overall, the fact that we find either no or little correlation between $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N and core properties confirm the chemical models of Roueff et al. ((cite: roueff15)) and Loison et al. ((cite: loison19)), in which enrichment in $^{15}$N is always very low or even negligible for all species formed in the gas phase like N$_{2}$H$^{+}$.

claims.hypothesis: The 14N/15N ratio in N2H+ is lower in dense embedded IRDC cores than in their surrounding diffuse gaseous envelopes, as expected from selective photodissociation.
claims.experiment: Measured N2H+ (1-0) and N15NH+ (1-0) column densities and 14N/15N ratios in compact 3 mm continuum cores using feathered 12m+7m+TP ALMA cubes (~3-4" resolution) and compared them to values derived from more extended N2H+ cores, ALMA Total Power data alone (~70" resolution), and prior single-dish surveys.
claims.result: In continuum cores, 14N/15N ranges from ~80 to ~400 (mean ~210), whereas Total Power data towards the same cores yield ratios a factor ~1.5-3 higher (280-500), and extended N2H+ cores have ratios similar to or up to ~1.5-2 times higher than embedded continuum cores (except F1-n2hp-1).
claims.finding: The 14N/15N ratio tends to be higher in the diffuse envelope than in dense embedded cores, consistent with selective photodissociation by external UV photons, although sensitivity limits preclude detecting ratios >400 at small scales.

evidence.quote: In all cores except F1c1, which is the most extended one, the beam-averaged $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratios are larger by a factor $\sim 1.5 - 3$ than those obtained in the embedded cores at higher angular resolution.

However, the sensitivity of our observations likely does not allow us to derive $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratios higher than $\sim 400$ at small scales. Therefore, higher sensitivity measurements will be absolutely required to confirm, or deny, this finding;

claims.hypothesis: Nitrogen fractionation in N2H+ varies with the evolutionary stage (starless vs star-forming) of IRDC cores.
claims.experiment: Compared the 14N/15N ratios measured in 5 starless and 12 star-forming 3 mm continuum cores classified via embedded infrared emission.
claims.result: The average 14N/15N ratio is ~190 in starless cores and ~220 in star-forming cores, with large dispersions.
claims.finding: Evolutionary stage (time) does not play a significant role in the enrichment or depletion of 15N in N2H+.

evidence.quote: The average $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio is slightly lower ($\sim 190$) in the starless cores than in the protostellar objects ($\sim 220$). However, given the large dispersions, we confirm overall the result suggested by previous works (Fontani et al. (cite: fontani15), Zeng et al. (cite: zeng17), Colzi et al. (cite: colzi18a), (cite: colzi18b)): time does not seem to play a role in the enrichment, or depletion, of $^{15}$N in N$_{2}$H$^{+}$.

claims.hypothesis: The 14N/15N ratio in IRDC cores correlates with core physical properties (radius, mass, dust temperature, sonic Mach number, virial parameter, volume density, and H2 column density).
claims.experiment: Performed non-parametric statistical tests and Pearson's r correlation analysis between 14N/15N and core physical parameters derived in Paper I for the 17 detected continuum cores.
claims.result: No strong correlations were found overall; tentative positive correlations were found with H2 column density (r ~ 0.54-0.61, p = 0.001-0.01) and, among star-forming cores only, with sonic Mach number (r ~ 0.76, p = 0.004) and dust temperature (r ~ 0.6, p = 0.04), heavily influenced by F1c1 and F1c2.
claims.finding: Little or no correlation exists between 14N/15N and core properties, confirming gas-phase chemical models predicting negligible 15N enrichment at T > 10 K, while tentative positive trends with column density, Mach number, and temperature may reflect selective photodissociation.

evidence.quote: Inspection of Figs. 6 and 7 suggests that, overall, there are no strong and clear (anti-)correlations between the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio and the analysed core properties. However, non-parametric statistical tests suggest very tentative positive correlations with the H$_2$ column density derived from the 3 mm continuum (in Fig. 7).

Overall, the fact that we find either no or little correlation between $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N and core properties confirm the chemical models of Roueff et al. ((cite: roueff15)) and Loison et al. ((cite: loison19)), in which enrichment in $^{15}$N is always very low or even negligible for all species formed in the gas phase like N$_{2}$H$^{+}$.

why_this_data.value: Previous single-dish surveys provided average 14N/15N values over ~0.1-1 pc scales that mix gas with different physical and chemical conditions; high-angular resolution interferometric observations with ALMA towards well-studied IRDCs are needed to resolve dense cores (<= 0.1 pc) and relate 14N/15N to core properties and star-formation activity.

evidence.quote: However, the observations mentioned above were obtained with single-dish telescopes, thus providing average values of the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio on linear scales of $\sim 0.1 - 1$ pc, which can contain gas with different conditions, due to the inner physical and chemical complexity of high-mass star-forming cores.

The $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio is derived from observations of N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ and N$^{15}$NH$^+$ (1–0) towards the dense cores of four clouds in which the physical and chemical structure has already been extensively studied at various wavelengths

why_this_method.value: Used 2D dendrogram contours on 3 mm continuum and N2H+ integrated intensity maps to focus on dense cores and N2H+ peaks given the faintness of N15NH+ and morphological complexity; integrated the isolated and weakest F1=0-1 hyperfine component of N2H+ (1-0) to minimize optical depth, self-absorption, and multiple velocity component blending.

evidence.quote: The faintness of the N$^{15}$NH$^+$ emission, and the large angular extension and morphological complexity of the target clouds, suggested us to focus the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N analysis first on the 3 mm continuum sources identified in each IRDC using the 2D dendrogram method (Rosolowsky et al. (cite: rosolowsky08)).

evidence.loc: 3.1.4 Derivation of the total column densities
evidence.quote: Therefore, we have estimated the N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ total column density, $N_{\rm tot}$(N$_{2}$H$^{+}$), from the integrated intensity of the hyperfine component F$_1 = 0-1$, which is well separated in velocity from the others and intrinsically the faintest one, and hence potentially the least affected by optical depth effects, self-absorption, or contribution of secondary faint velocity features.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Showing integrated intensity maps of N15NH+ (1-0) was rejected due to the faintness of the N15NH+ lines.

evidence.quote: Due to the faintness of the N$^{15}$NH$^+$ lines, we do not show integrated maps of the N$^{15}$NH$^+$ emission.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Fitting the full hyperfine structure of N15NH+ (1-0) was rejected in all but four cores because the satellite components were undetected.

evidence.quote: In all but four cores, D5c5/6/7, F1C3, F4c5, and F4c7, the hyperfine structure cannot be fitted because the satellites are undetected. Therefore, the main components have been fitted with a single Gaussian

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Deriving N2H+ column densities from full hyperfine structure fits was rejected because complex line profiles (multiple velocity components, self-absorption, and optical depth) yielded high fit residuals.

evidence.loc: 3.1.4 Derivation of the total column densities
evidence.quote: The complexity of the N$_{2}$H$^{+}$(1–0) line profiles, clearly seen in the spectra of Figs. 8 – 11, and described in Sect. 3.1.3, makes it difficult to obtain fits with low residuals. Therefore, we have estimated the N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ total column density, $N_{\rm tot}$(N$_{2}$H$^{+}$), from the integrated intensity of the hyperfine component F$_1 = 0-1$

limitations_admitted.value: Sensitivity of the ALMA observations does not allow detection of N15NH+ in cores with 14N/15N higher than ~400, so it is uncertain whether the narrower range of 14N/15N compared to single-dish studies is partly due to limited sensitivity.

evidence.quote: This means that our interferometric observations are not sensitive to N$^{15}$NH$^+$ emission in cores with $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N higher than $\sim 400$, and hence we cannot conclude if the narrower range of isotopic ratios measured in this work depends also on our limited sensitivity.

limitations_admitted.value: Non-negligible optical depth or self-absorption in the F1=0-1 component of N2H+ (1-0) can lead to underestimating N_tot(N2H+) and the 14N/15N ratio (e.g., in D6c6, D7c1, D7c2, and H5c3).

evidence.loc: 3.1.4 Derivation of the total column densities
evidence.quote: when the line profile was attributed more likely to self-absorption (e.g. in the cores D6c6, D7c1 and D7c2), we have integrated the whole component, bearing in mind that this will provide a lower limit on $N_{\rm tot}$(N$_{2}$H$^{+}$), and hence a lower limit on the associated $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N as well.

Another caveat on the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratios arises from the possible non negligible optical depth of the F$_1=0-1$ component of N$_{2}$H$^{+}$(1–0), which could lead us to underestimate $N_{\rm tot}$(N$_{2}$H$^{+}$) and, from this, the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio.

limitations_admitted.value: Low number of N2H+ cores associated with N2D+ cores and detected in N15NH+ (only 4) prevents statistical analysis of the relation between nitrogen and deuterium fractionation.

evidence.quote: A few of them are indeed associated, but unfortunately only 4 of those are also detected in N$^{15}$NH$^+$, and thus the statistics is too low to discuss possible relations between nitrogen and deuterium fractionation.

limitations_admitted.value: Starless cores may not be truly pre-stellar or may contain unresolved star-forming fragments undetected in IR images.

evidence.quote: In fact, first the nature of our starless cores could not be "pre–stellar" but just starless or star-forming in a very early stage of star-formation activity; second, some cores are extended and could contain smaller fragments in different evolutionary stages.

limitations_admitted.value: Tentative correlations with core properties are strongly influenced by two sources (F1c1 and F1c2), rely on low S/N (3-5 sigma) N15NH+ detections, and use Herschel dust temperatures measured at coarser angular resolution than the individual cores.

evidence.quote: However, all trends are strongly influenced by sources F1c1 and F1c2 (Figs. 6 and 7). Moreover, most N$^{15}$NH$^+$ lines are detected with a signal to noise ratio in between 3 and 5, and hence any trend that can be found from the plots in Figs. 6 and 7 must be taken with caution.

However, the temperature of our cores at the scales studied by us is always above $\sim 10$ K, in agreement with the lack of $^{15}$N enrichment, although the temperature measurement is taken over an angular scale (i.e. the Herschel beam) larger than that of the individual cores.

referee_caveats_inferred: Dependence on an unpublished companion paper (Barnes et al. in prep., Paper I) for core coordinates, angular sizes, continuum dendrogram parameters, and core physical properties makes standalone verification of the extracted spectra and correlation plots impossible without external data.

Assuming optically thin emission for the F1=0-1 hyperfine component of N2H+ (1-0) in high-column-density IRDC cores systematically biases N_tot(N2H+) and 14N/15N downward when tau(F1=0-1) is moderate to high, as demonstrated by the factor of ~1.7 correction in H5c3.
